newsitem.title: USA: Forest Oil plans 2 deepwater wildcats.
newsitem.headline: Forest Oil plans 2 deepwater wildcats.

text.p: Forest Oil Corp plans to start two deepwater wildcats in the Gulf of Mexico this year, chief executive Robert S. Boswell said Tuesday.
He told the EnerCOM/San Jacinto Securities Boston Energy Conference that Forest's strategy in North America maintains a balance between lower-risk and high-impact exploration.

The company will continue to drill lower-risk targets on the continental shelf in the Gulf of Mexico, in the Western Sedimentary Basin in the U.S. and in Western Canada, but also has begun developing prospects in the deeper water of the Gulf and in Canada's Northwest Territories, he explained.
On East Breaks Block 164, in which the company has a 100 percent working interest, the company plans its first venture into the Gulf of Mexico's deeper water, Boswell said.
The block is in offshore Texas in 700 feet of water. An exploratory well is planned for later this year.
Another attractive opportunity for Forest, he said, is the Ewing Banks Block 350 in offshore Louisiana, in which the company also has a 100 percent working interest.
This lease is in about 800 feet of water and sits in the Timbalier Trench, where the Mississippi River flows into the Gulf of Mexico. A test well is planned for late 1997.
Boswell also noted Forest's current production is about 132 million cubic feet of natural gas and 7,600 barrels of oil per day. ((-- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.))
